transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ChatGPT. What brings you in today?

For years now I’ve felt this constant heaviness and sadness that never really lifts, even when things in my life are going okay. It just feels like a persistent weight I can't seem to shake off, no matter how hard I try to keep up appearances.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months when you felt back to your usual self, or has this low mood been present most days for years without much relief?

No, I haven't had any periods of relief like that at all. This heavy, low mood has been constant and steady for the last three years, ever since my husband and I separated. I haven't felt back to my usual self for even a couple of weeks, let alone two months.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F34.1, F32.9, F33.9], but the patient now describes a continuous low mood for three years with no symptom-free interval of at least two months. This makes a recurrent depressive disorder less likely because there is no evidence of distinct episodes, and a single depressive episode is less likely because the presentation is chronic and persistent rather than time-limited. The current candidate is therefore the persistent depressive disorder code.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronic depressed mood with persistent sadness/heaviness for 3 years, occurring most days without any symptom-free interval of 2 months or more, which is most consistent with dysthymia (persistent depressive disorder). The history does not establish discrete major depressive episodes or remission patterns needed to favor recurrent or single depressive episode diagnoses.
